title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
description: Ten documented University Library study environments across campus, spanning quiet reading rooms, collaborative tables, and technology-focused spaces.

cards.title: ACES (Funk) Library Floors 2–4
cards.subtitle: ACES Library, 1101 S. Goodwin Ave., Urbana
cards.notes: Settle into the upper library floors when natural light matters. Bring a covered drink and use the six reservable rooms for planned group work.
cards.short_summary: A large, naturally lit library setting with both open seating and reservable rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: The University Library lists ACES (Funk) Library floors 2–4 as a 350-person study area with extensive natural light, covered drinks allowed, and six reservable rooms.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces Throughout the University Library
cards.access_notes: University Library study-space directory lists this location; check current library access and building hours before visiting.

cards.title: Communications Library Room 39
cards.subtitle: Gregory Hall, Room 39
cards.notes: Use this Gregory Hall room for conversation-friendly work. Its listed activity level suits a project meeting or a study session with spoken discussion.
cards.short_summary: A communications-library room designed for active, collaborative study.
cards.evidence_claim: The University Library lists Communications Library Room 39 in Gregory Hall as a 51-person, volume-level-3 study space with natural and overhead lighting; covered drinks are allowed.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces Throughout the University Library
cards.access_notes: University Library study-space directory lists this location; check current library access and building hours before visiting.

cards.title: Communications Library Room 122
cards.subtitle: Gregory Hall, Room 122
cards.notes: Choose Room 122 for a smaller Gregory Hall session with daylight. Keep a covered drink handy and plan for a lower conversation level than Room 39.
cards.short_summary: A 40-seat, daylight-supported study room in the Communications Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The University Library lists Communications Library Room 122 in Gregory Hall as a 40-person, volume-level-2 study space with natural and overhead lighting; covered drinks are allowed.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces Throughout the University Library
cards.access_notes: University Library study-space directory lists this location; check current library access and building hours before visiting.

cards.title: Grainger 1 West Design Space
cards.subtitle: Grainger Engineering Library Information Center, 1 West
cards.notes: Bring collaborators and working materials to this design-focused floor area. Food and drinks are permitted, and its listed activity level accommodates project noise.
cards.short_summary: A 120-seat Grainger setting intended for lively, design-oriented collaboration.
cards.evidence_claim: The University Library lists Grainger Engineering Library's 1 West Design Space as a 120-person, volume-level-4 area where food and drink are welcome.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces Throughout the University Library
cards.access_notes: University Library study-space directory lists this location; check current Grainger Library access and hours before visiting.

cards.title: SSHEL Main Library Room 101
cards.subtitle: Social Sciences, Health, and Education Library, Main Library Room 101
cards.notes: Use the large-window seating in Room 101 for individual work with a conversational background. Keep beverages covered as required by the library listing.
cards.short_summary: A 67-seat SSHEL study area with ample window light.
cards.evidence_claim: The University Library lists SSHEL Main Library Room 101 as a 67-person, volume-level-2 study space with substantial natural light; covered drinks are allowed.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces Throughout the University Library
cards.access_notes: University Library study-space directory lists this location; check current Main Library access and hours before visiting.

cards.title: SSHEL Main Library Room 123
cards.subtitle: Social Sciences, Health, and Education Library, Main Library Room 123
cards.notes: Pick this compact SSHEL room when you need quiet shelves nearby. Talking is discouraged; bring only a covered drink and keep phone calls outside.
cards.short_summary: A 26-seat, low-volume SSHEL study area among the stacks.
cards.evidence_claim: The University Library lists SSHEL Main Library Room 123 as a 26-person, volume-level-1 study space with light from windows and overhead fixtures; covered drinks are allowed.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces Throughout the University Library
cards.access_notes: University Library study-space directory lists this location; check current Main Library access and hours before visiting.

cards.title: The Orange Room
cards.subtitle: Teaching, Learning, and Academic Support, Main Library Rooms 100 and 112
cards.notes: Set up at the large tables for solo or team work, then reserve a study room if needed. Power outlets, printers, and short-term technology loans are nearby.
cards.short_summary: A bright first-floor hub with tables, power, reservable rooms, and library support nearby.
cards.evidence_claim: The University Library describes the Orange Room in Main Library rooms 100 and 112 as a large study space with large tables, ample power, reservable study rooms, printers, and short-term technology loans.
cards.access_notes: Located on the first floor of the Main Library; study rooms are reservable. Check current Main Library access and hours before visiting.

cards.title: Shebik Family Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Literature & Languages Library, Main Library
cards.notes: Bring reading or writing work to this low-volume room. Table lamps and indirect light offer an alternative to bright overhead-only study areas.
cards.short_summary: A 320-seat reading room combining natural light, table lamps, and a quiet-use expectation.
cards.evidence_claim: The University Library lists the Shebik Family Reading Room in the Literature & Languages Library as a 320-person, volume-level-1 study space with natural light, table lamps, and low indirect lighting.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces Throughout the University Library
cards.access_notes: University Library study-space directory lists this location; check current Main Library access and hours before visiting.

cards.title: Central Access Services Room 204
cards.subtitle: Main Library Room 204
cards.notes: Use Room 204 for a study group that benefits from natural light and historic chandeliers. Food and drinks are allowed in this active-use Main Library space.
cards.short_summary: A 67-seat Main Library space pairing daylight with historic fixtures.
cards.evidence_claim: The University Library lists Central Access Services Main Library Room 204 as a 67-person, volume-level-3 study space with natural light and historic chandeliers; food and drink are welcome.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces Throughout the University Library
cards.access_notes: University Library study-space directory lists this location; check current Main Library access and hours before visiting.

cards.title: Media Commons Room 220
cards.subtitle: Main Library Room 220
cards.notes: Choose this media-oriented room for a group session requiring daylight and nearby reservable rooms. Use a covered drink and expect an active environment.
cards.short_summary: An 83-seat Media Commons study space with daylight and four reservable rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: The University Library lists Media Commons Main Library Room 220 as an 83-person, volume-level-4 study space with substantial natural light and four reservable rooms; covered drinks are allowed.
cards.source_title: Study Spaces Throughout the University Library
cards.access_notes: University Library study-space directory lists this location and four reservable rooms; check current Main Library access and hours before visiting.
